title: data/slugs.json
description: The frozen URL slug of every actor ever published. An actor keeps its slug when its name or its member records change, and a slug that stops naming an actor is kept as a retired entry, so no address is reused or silently lost. It lives beside the other data files, not under actors/, because it is not an actor page.

entries.description: One entry per slug ever published, sorted by slug.

slugEntry.description: One slug and what is needed to recognise the actor that owns it in the next build.

slug.description: The actor's ID and URL segment. It never changes once published. An ATT&CK group's slug is its group ID.

display_name.description: The name the actor page showed in the last build that published it. Only a note for readers of this file; a changed name never changes the slug.

anchors.description: The published member records of the actor, as source:source_id, or the bare ATT&CK group ID, sorted. A later build recognises the actor by any anchor it still shares. They are record identifiers, never alias names, so a name a page does not show cannot appear here.

first_published.description: The date of the build that first gave out this slug. When two entries merge, the older one keeps its slug.

suffix.description: The number added to the slug because the natural slug was already owned, or null when none was needed. The slug then ends in a hyphen and this number.

retired.description: True when no published actor owns the slug in the last build. A retired slug is never given to another actor.

merged_into.description: The slug of the actor this one was merged into, or null. Only a retired entry has one, and it names the end of any chain of merges. It is what the retired page links to.

actorId.description: An ATT&CK group ID such as G0007, or a lower-case ASCII slug for an actor ATT&CK does not track. The ID is also the actor's file name and URL segment, so it has no colons, slashes or spaces, and it is never 'index'.

label.description: Non-empty text with no leading or trailing whitespace and no line breaks.

buildDate.description: A build date, YYYY-MM-DD, never earlier than 1990.
